main_text.p: fit,& exitiofum ,summam neceffario poftu lac medici curam ac diligentiam. An verò rabiofi canis morfus fit, aut alius animalis in primis percunctandum eft nobis : quòd facile perceperis nucibus regijs probe tri-tis,& inflicto ulceri impofitis, quas poftri-die gallo gallinaceo, aut gallinae edendas offeres.Primum quidem ipfas non contin-get.Quòd fi urgente fame eas ederit, atten-dito.Nam fi non rabiofus fit canis , qui ho-minem momordit, viuet gallus, qui edit, fin rabiofus poftridie morietur. Tuc ulcus præpropere aperies medicamento ex pi-ce,aceto acerrimo ,& oppopanace parato. Si vero tenera cute fuerit, qui morfus eft, irino oleo, aut aliquo huiufmodi refoluen-tium diluatur:aut fotu urinae fani hominis prius adhibito ulcus allio integito. Serue-tur autem ulcus apertu, nullaq; cicatrice obductum ad dies quadraginta duos. Non pretermiisis omnibus alijs medicamentis ad hoc virus expugnandum fpeftantibus, unum fummum ac primum, nempe cinere fluuiatilium cancrorum tum a veteribus, tum etiam a recentioribus tantopere cele-bratum,præscribere nobis visum eft. page.notes: Printed "Tuc" in "Tuc ulcus" is probably an abbreviated "Tunc"; transcribed as printed. "irino oleo" is doubtful (possibly a misprint for another word). Printed "pretermiisis" has a doubled i, left as printed. "eft," at the foot is a catchword for the next page. The page is one continuous paragraph carried over from the previous page; no paragraph break is visible.
